alt: A source grid and an empty target grid of swapped dimensions. Each source cell moves to the target at n minus one minus column and row, filling the target one cell at a time.

steps.caption: The source is 2 rows by 3 columns. The target has 3 rows by 2 columns, every cell still marked ?, because rotating 90 degrees swaps the dimensions.
old[0][0] = 1 moves to new[2][0]: a counterclockwise turn sends column 0 to row 2, and row 0 to column 0.
Next, old[0][1] = 2 lands at new[1][0], following the same rule.
Next, old[0][2] = 3 lands at new[0][0], following the same rule.
Next, old[1][0] = 4 lands at new[2][1], following the same rule.
Next, old[1][1] = 5 lands at new[1][1], following the same rule.
Next, old[1][2] = 6 lands at new[0][1], following the same rule.
Every source cell has moved. The target is the source rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise.
The source is 3 rows by 1 columns. The target has 1 rows by 3 columns, every cell still marked ?, because rotating 90 degrees swaps the dimensions.
old[0][0] = 7 moves to new[0][0]: a counterclockwise turn sends column 0 to row 0, and row 0 to column 0.
Next, old[1][0] = 8 lands at new[0][1], following the same rule.
Next, old[2][0] = 9 lands at new[0][2], following the same rule.
Every source cell has moved. The target is the source rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise.
